subject: Throughput anchoring request & queueing priority during launch
messages:
From: Asha Mehra <asha@novaedge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novaedge.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: request to anchor throughput for launch

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood Dedicated. As we map the launch plan for our recommendation engine (expected traffic spike week-of Oct 18), procurement asked me to surface one technical ask up front: can Redwood provide a short-term throughput anchoring guarantee for the first 30 days post-launch and a temporary queueing priority to reduce throttling during the initial ramp?

Specifics:
- Target baseline: 60 tokens/sec sustained for our reserved pool (model: rw-large-quant) with 15% headroom for 30 days.
- Queueing behavior: for critical production routes (predict-api, rerank-api) we’d like non-preemptible in-flight requests for the first 2 weeks of launch and a prioritized soft-lane for the following 2 weeks.

We understand this is outside standard reserved-GPU terms — happy to discuss tradeoffs, credits, or limited-duration fees. Procurement also asked for contract language so they can circulate a redline quickly.

Can you confirm feasibility and next steps?

Thanks,
Asha
Asha Mehra
Head of Product, NovaEdge Analytics
asha@novaedge.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Mehra <asha@novaedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: request to anchor throughput for launch

Hi Asha — great to hear NovaEdge is on track. Quick read: yes, we can support a time-bound anchoring approach but there are a couple of operational constraints to align on. High-level proposal:

1) 30-day throughput anchor: we can reserve the requested baseline (60 t/s) and provide a 15% headroom buffer for 30 days. That maps to a soft buffer token allowance on top of committed capacity; beyond that we’ll apply burst pricing.

2) Queueing/priority: we can enable a temporary prioritized soft-lane for the two production routes. Making in-flight requests non-preemptible for all reserved GPUs is tougher across a multi-tenant rack — instead we can guarantee non-preemptible behavior for those specific API routes by routing to a pinned subset of the pool (cost implication: ~1.2x reserved capacity during the window).

3) Contract language: attaching a short addendum draft and a runbook matrix to show the exact time-window, metrics, and rollback controls. If that looks OK I’ll route to legal for a narrow-term SOW and give procurement a DocuSign link.

Next steps I suggest:
- Marissa, can you confirm cost delta for the pinned subset and produce an estimate?
- Karthik, can you outline the operational runbook for priority lanes and eviction rules so Asha’s team can review?

Asha — can you confirm the exact launch date window and whether the 30 days must be contiguous from first traffic event or a calendar window?

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Asha Mehra <asha@novaedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 14:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: request to anchor throughput for launch

Ben — I ran a quick cost simulation. Summary:
- Baseline reserved pool to support 60 t/s + 15% headroom for 30 days requires adding ~0.25 reserved GPUs (effectively rounding up to one extra node in most zones).
- Pinning a subset of the pool for non-preemptible in-flight for two weeks increases the effective reserved commitment by ~20% for that window (we size by concurrent inflight slots).

Estimate (rough): $16,500 additional for the full 30 day anchoring + $4,200 incremental to cover the two-week pinned lane; we can convert these into credits if legal prefers crediting vs separate invoice line.

I’ll formalize numbers into the addendum if you want to proceed; Ben, please confirm whether we should propose credits or a short-term surcharge.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Mehra <asha@novaedge.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: request to anchor throughput for launch

Asha — technical notes on the runbook (summary):
- Priority lanes will be implemented via routing policy + small pinned replica set. We’ll instruct the router to prefer pinned replicas for requests with route tag (predict-api / rerank-api) for the two-week window.
- Eviction policy during the pinned window: pinned replicas will accept in-flight token caching and KV affinity; we’ll prevent preemption for inflight tokens but background batch jobs may still be scheduled on separate nodes to avoid starving the pool.
- Failover: if pinned replica health drops below 90% for >5 minutes we’ll automatically shift traffic to the broader pool and trigger a rollback to standard priority + crediting for affected minutes.
- Observability hooks: we’ll open an SLO dashboard for NovaEdge with token/sec, p95 latency, preemption events (boolean), and a rolling count of queued requests.

I’ve added the specifics into the runbook file attached earlier. Happy to hop on a short call with your ops team to walk the sequence.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Asha Mehra <asha@novaedge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novaedge.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: request to anchor throughput for launch

Ben / team — this is very helpful, thanks. Procurement reviewed the addendum and prefers credits over an invoice line (keeps our accounting simpler). Two quick clarifications before we send legal the redline:
- Confirmed: 30 contiguous days starting at first production traffic event (we’ll send a call when we flip).
- Can you add a clause that caps NovaEdge financial exposure for excess burst beyond the 15% headroom to a not-to-exceed amount ($12,000)?

If you can incorporate those two items into the addendum we can route to DocuSign today. Also yes, please set up the SLO dashboard and a 30-min technical run-through with our ops on Sept 10.

Asha
Asha Mehra
Head of Product, NovaEdge Analytics
